messages:
secops: :rotating_light: High priority: support bundle sb-2026-04-01-09 included an SSH agent socket and agent-forwarded keys were present in the archive. Treat any keys accessible via agent as potentially used and rotate where possible.

nate (support): Confirmed. The bundle contained /tmp/ssh-XXXX/agent. I quarantined the object and removed public access immediately. Vendor may have pulled it before we blocked.

riley (infra): How did the socket get bundled? Our collector should ignore sockets and /tmp.

tasha (dev): Root cause: the support collector uses 'tar -cf' over the whole runtime directory which included mounted /tmp with active ssh-agent sockets. An ephemeral socket file got packaged.

sam (oncall): Quick detection commands for teams to run on builder/host machines and unpacked bundles:
```
# locate agent sockets
find / -type s -name "ssh-*" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,200p'
# inspect a bundle for socket-like entries
tar -tf support-bundle.tar.gz | rg "ssh-[0-9a-zA-Z\-]+/agent" || true
```

legal-bot: If the vendor downloaded the bundle, Legal needs the download logs and vendor contact. Preserve chain-of-custody.

secops: Action items: 
- Immediate: Rotate any deploy keys and credentials that were proxied by ssh-agent on affected hosts. Treat forwarded keys as compromised even if private key file not present.
- Contain: Confirm deleted/quarantined S3 object and enable object-level logging for the bucket.
- Patch: Update support collector to exclude socket files, /tmp, and anything matching pattern 'ssh-*'. Use a scrubber to fail uploads that contain special file types (sockets, fifos).
- Audit: Search last 60 days of support bundles and artifact archives for socket entries and flag for rotation.
- Policy: Disable agent-forwarding in default SSH configs on build hosts and add preflight check to CI images.

nate (support): I've disabled uploads to external vendors until the scrubber patch lands. MR #7422 will add the filter and a tar --exclude for sockets. Rolling to canary in 20m.

riley (infra): I've pushed a temporary firewall rule to prevent external IPs from accessing builder hosts and added a host-level cron to kill lingering ssh-agent processes after CI runs. Also created incident tag 'sec-2498765432'.

tasha (dev): We'll update developer docs: never enable SSH agent forwarding on shared build hosts. MR #7423 to add agent-forwarding hardening and a startup check.

sam (oncall): Example rotation steps for deploy keys and SSH access: 
```
# identify keys currently loaded in agent (if you still have session)
ssh-add -l
# remove old key from hosts and replace authorized_keys with new pubkey
ssh user@host "sed -i '/oldkeypub/d' ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && cat new.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
```

secops: Deadline: discovery and rotations for any keys referenced by detected sockets within 48 hours. Post confirmation in this thread. If vendor confirms download and cannot delete, escalate to Legal and Comms.

legal-bot: Legal requested vendor logs and will advise on disclosure if external parties accessed any systems with those keys. Nate, DM me the vendor contact and download timestamps.

nate (support): Vendor confirms single download, provided access log (agent@vendor.example.com). Sending to Legal now.

riley (infra): Audit across support buckets found 3 additional bundles with socket entries in the last 30 days. Marking them for quarantine and initiating rotations for any associated services.

tasha (dev): Patch merged to canary collector; scrubber rejects sockets and special files. Adding CI test to assert no sockets are present in produced bundles.

secops: New policy: effective immediately, builds and support collectors must not include device files or sockets. Automation and a short guidance doc will be published in 72h. React with :rotating_light: if you need a war-room call.

sam (oncall): Scans are in progress; will post high-priority hits to SEC-2498765432.
